newsitem.title: CHINA: China repeats ban on overseas futures trading.
newsitem.headline: China repeats ban on overseas futures trading.

text.p: China's top market watchdog has repeated a ban on futures trading overseas and margin trading of foreign exchange after firms were found to have continued to engage in such activity, official securities newspapers said on Saturday.
The China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) issued the directive to maintain financial order and protect social stability, the newspapers said.
Some institutions recently made such trades under the guise of consulting companies or investment advisory firms, they said, quoting the CSRC directive.
"The embers of illegal overseas futures and foreign exchange margin trading are still smouldering," the Shanghai Securities News said. It gave no specific cases.

Regulators will shut down companies that engage in these types of trading and confiscate their income, the directive said. Futures brokerages that carry out such trading will be barred from the industry, it said.

China allows only designated state-backed companies to use overseas futures market to hedge their positions and bans margin trading of foreign exchange, which allows trading without having to settle the full amount by the use of a special account.
Beijing in the past three years has carried out periodic crackdowns on its domestic futures market as well as futures trading overseas in a bid to halt speculation.
